arxiv-1711-01028.title: High brightness fully coherent X-ray amplifier seeded by a free-electron laser oscillator
arxiv-1711-01028.creator: Kai Li 1,2, Jiawei Yan 1,2, Chao Feng 1, Meng Zhang 1, Haixiao Deng 1,
arxiv-1711-01028.description: Abstract X-ray free-electron laser oscillator (XFELO) is expected to be a cutting edge tool for fully coherent X-ray laser generation, and undulator taper technique is well-known for considerably increasing the efficiency of free-electron lasers (FELs). In order to combine the advantages of these two schemes, FEL amplifier seeded by XFELO is proposed by simply using a chirped electron beam.

arxiv-2304-04756.title: Asymptotic states and S S -matrix operator in de Sitter ambient space formalism
arxiv-2304-04756.creator: M.V. Takook, J.P. Gazeau, E. Huguet
arxiv-2304-04756.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M.V. Takook, J.P. Gazeau, E. Huguet. Within the de Sitter ambient space framework, the two different bases of the one-particle Hilbert space of the de Sitter group algebra are presented for the scalar case. Using field operator algebra and its Fock space construction in this formalism, we discuss the existence of asymptotic states in de Sitter QFT under an extension of the adiabatic hypothesis and prove the Fock space completeness theorem for the massive scalar field.

arxiv-2308-08200.title: Towards Ontology-Mediated Planning with OWL DL Ontologies (Extended Version)
arxiv-2308-08200.creator: Tobias John, Patrick Koopmann
arxiv-2308-08200.description: Abstract While classical planning languages make the closed-domain and closed-world assumption, there have been various approaches to extend those with DL reasoning, which is then interpreted under the usual open-world semantics. Current approaches for planning with DL ontologies integrate the DL directly into the planning language, and practical approaches have been developed based on first-order rewritings or rewritings into datalog.

arxiv-2310-14633.title: Extending Input Contexts of Language Models through Training on Segmented Sequences
arxiv-2310-14633.creator: Petros Karypis, Julian McAuley, George Karypis
arxiv-2310-14633.description: Abstract Effectively training language models on long inputs poses many technical challenges. As a cost consideration, languages models are pretrained on a fixed sequence length before being adapted to longer sequences. We explore various methods for adapting models to longer inputs by training on segmented sequences and an interpolation-based method for extending absolute positional embeddings.

arxiv-2411-06188.title: Lorentz violation and Hawking–Page metastability in Bumblebee–AdS gravity
arxiv-2411-06188.creator: Syed Masood
arxiv-2411-06188.description: Abstract The standard Hawking–Page description of AdS black holes, based on an on-shell Gibbs free-energy crossing, does not resolve the metastable black-hole branch or the barrier-mediated conversion between competing phases. We address this issue for neutral AdS black holes in Bumblebee gravity by constructing the generalized off-shell Gibbs free-energy landscape in the canonical ensemble at fixed effective pressure.

arxiv-2501-01679.title: Adaptive Few-shot Prompting for Machine Translation with Pre-trained Language Models
arxiv-2501-01679.creator: Lei Tang, Jinghui Qin, Wenxuan Ye, Hao Tan, Zhijing Yang
arxiv-2501-01679.description: Abstract Recently, Large language models (LLMs) with in-context learning have demonstrated remarkable potential in handling neural machine translation. However, existing evidence shows that LLMs are prompt-sensitive and it is sub-optimal to apply the fixed prompt to any input for downstream machine translation tasks.

arxiv-2601-06695.title: Nonparametric contaminated Gaussian mixture of regressions
arxiv-2601-06695.creator: Sphiwe B. Skhosana 1* and Weixin Yao 2 1 Department of Statistics, University of Pretoria, Pretoria, 0028, South Africa 2 Department of Statistics, University of California, Riverside, CA, USA * Corresponding author: spiwe.skhosana@up.ac.za
arxiv-2601-06695.description: Abstract Semi- and non-parametric mixture of regressions are a very useful flexible class of mixture of regressions in which some or all of the parameters are non-parametric functions of the covariates. These models are, however, based on the Gaussian assumption of the component error distributions. Thus, their estimation is sensitive to outliers and heavy-tailed error distributions.

arxiv-2601-07403.title: Modeling and analysis of a novel two-strain dengue epidemics model considering secondary infections with increased mortality
arxiv-2601-07403.creator: Burcu Gürbüz, Aytül Gökçe, Joseph Páez Chávez, Thomas Götz
arxiv-2601-07403.description: Abstract In this study, we develop and analyze a deterministic two-strain host–vector model for dengue transmission that incorporates key immuno-epidemiological mechanisms, including temporary cross-immunity, antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), disease-induced mortality during secondary infections, and explicit vector co-infection. The human population is divided into compartments for primary and secondary infections, while the mosquito population includes single- and co-infected classes.

pmc-10566684.title: Adenylosuccinate lyase deficiency affects neurobehavior via perturbations to tyramine signaling in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-10566684.creator: Corinna A. Moro, Sabrina A. Sony, Latisha P. Franklin, Shirley Dong, Mia M. Peifer, Kathryn E. Wittig, Wendy Hanna-Rose
pmc-10566684.description: Adenylosuccinate lyase deficiency is an ultrarare congenital metabolic disorder associated with muscle weakness and neurobehavioral dysfunction. Adenylosuccinate lyase is required for de novo purine biosynthesis, acting twice in the pathway at non-sequential steps. Genetic models can contribute to our understanding of the etiology of disease phenotypes and pave the way for development of therapeutic treatments.

pmc-10626043.title: Vertebro-Vertebral Fistula Occlusion Using a Woven EndoBridgeTM-Device
pmc-10626043.creator: Rasmus Holmboe Dahl, Mohammad Ghasemi-Rad, Vagn Eskesen, Susanne Christiansen Frevert, Christine Sølling, Goetz Benndorf
pmc-10626043.description: Vertebro-vertebral fistulas (VVFs) are vascular lesions that may develop after trauma or spontaneously in association with connective tissue disorders. We present a rare case of a post-traumatic VVF in a young patient presenting with a painless swelling and a bruit in her left upper neck.

pmc-11406653.title: The Impact of Triglyceride-Glucose Index Levels During Perioperative Period on Outcomes in Femoral Neck Fracture Patients
pmc-11406653.creator: Sezer Astan, Orhan Balta
pmc-11406653.description: IntroductionThe objective of the present study is to assess the impact of the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG index) on the prognosis and explore the correlation between the TyG index and all-cause mortality in femoral neck fracture patients.Materials and MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed the TyG index in the follow-up of femoral neck fracture patients who underwent partial hip prosthesis.

pmc-11495929.title: Predicting 30-day mortality in severely injured elderly patients with trauma in Korea using machine learning algorithms: a retrospective study
pmc-11495929.creator: Jonghee Han, Su Young Yoon, Junepill Seok, Jin Young Lee, Jin Suk Lee, Jin Bong Ye, Younghoon Sul, Se Heon Kim, Hong Rye Kim
pmc-11495929.description: PurposeThe number of elderly patients with trauma is increasing; therefore, precise models are necessary to estimate the mortality risk of elderly patients with trauma for informed clinical decision-making. This study aimed to develop machine learning based predictive models that predict 30-day mortality in severely injured elderly patients with trauma and to compare the predictive performance of various machine learning models.

pmc-11637769.title: A cyclical marker system enables indefinite series of oligonucleotide-directed gene editing in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
pmc-11637769.creator: Ian L Ross, Hong Phuong Le, Sabar Budiman, Dake Xiong, Fritz Hemker, Elizabeth A Millen, Melanie Oey, Ben Hankamer
pmc-11637769.description: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing in the model green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii relies on the use of selective marker genes to enrich for nonselectable target mutations. This becomes challenging when many sequential modifications are required in a single-cell line, as useful markers are limited.

pmc-11656856.title: Transcriptome-aligned metabolic profiling by SERSome reflects biological changes following mesenchymal stem cells expansion
pmc-11656856.creator: Xinyuan Bi, Bin Ma, Wei Liu, Wei-Qiang Gao, Jian Ye, Hanyu Rao
pmc-11656856.description: BackgroundMesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are widely applied in the treatment of various clinical diseases and in the field of medical aesthetics. However, MSCs exhibit greater heterogeneity limited stability, and more complex molecular and mechanistic characteristics compared to conventional drugs, making rapid and precise monitoring more challenging.

pmc-11715955.title: Impact of TBI on AD‐Associated Proteins in Neuron‐Derived Small Extracellular Vesicles from the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging
pmc-11715955.creator: Michaela Cullum‐Doyle, Matthew S Panizzon, Victoria Risbrough, Sonal Sukreet, Haoyi Yang, Jeremy A Elman, Carol E Franz, William S Kremen, Robert A Rissman
pmc-11715955.description: BackgroundAlzheimer's Disease (AD) and traumatic brain injuries (TBI) are frequently associated in medical literature, with a significant prevalence of TBI history observed among individuals diagnosed with AD. Our investigation focuses on this intersection, explicitly examining the risk of AD in individuals with a history of TBI.

pmc-12562642.title: Simultaneous Accumulation of Holocellulose, Callose and Lignin: Cell Wall Markers for Resistance in Wheat Infested with Diuraphis noxia
pmc-12562642.creator: Siphephelo N. N. Zondo, Lintle Mohase, Vicki Tolmay, Mpho Mafa
pmc-12562642.description: Exposure of the plant cell wall to biotic and abiotic stresses results in structural and chemical changes. Russian wheat aphid (RWA) infestation severely damages wheat plants, releasing cell wall-degrading enzymes that compromise cell wall integrity. This study aims to elucidate the cell wall modifications in resistant wheat cultivars during RWA infestation.

pmc-12583687.title: RNA sequencing reveals novel lncRNA modulators in gemini nanocurcumin–treated colorectal cancer cells
pmc-12583687.creator: Zohre Zibaei, Hewa Jalal Azeez, Esmaeil Babaei
pmc-12583687.description: Due to a high rate of recurrence coupled with resistance towards modern therapies, colorectal cancer (CRC) is considered as the third cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Gemini curcumin (Gemini-Cur) is one of the last nanoformulation of curcumin with significant toxicity on colorectal cancer.

pmc-12799703.title: Development and validation of a risk-based nomogram for predicting peritoneal dialysis catheter dysfunction in end-stage renal disease patients
pmc-12799703.creator: Bin Zhao, Shanshan Guo, Wei Li, Hongqing Shang, Yutao Xing, Jing Liu, Yanwei Hu, Yuzhu Wang, Gang Fu
pmc-12799703.description: BackgroundPeritoneal dialysis catheter (PDC) dysfunction significantly impacts patient survival. While individual risk factors are known, a practical tool that integrates multi-dimensional predictors—including surgical, anatomical, and postoperative parameters—for early risk stratification is lacking. This study evaluates open versus laparoscopic catheterization techniques and aims to develop such a predictive model.

pmc-13271149.title: Building bridges between brain and behavior: An open-source toolbox for joint modeling with fMRI
pmc-13271149.creator: Niek Stevenson, Steven Miletić, Birte U. Forstmann

pmc-13416917.title: Beyond acceptance: bounded use of AI and VR in orthopedic education
pmc-13416917.creator: Xiaohong Lyu, Yiwei Zhao, Siyi Cai, Jianguo Zhang
pmc-13416917.description: BackgroundThe educational roles of artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual reality (VR) in orthopedic training remain insufficiently defined. Rather than examining acceptance alone, we investigated how students delineate trust boundaries, role allocation, and implementation priorities for bounded, faculty-supervised use of AI/VR in orthopedic education.

pmc-13564652.title: Effects of Test-Section Length and Cross-Sectional Blockage on the Swimming Performance of Juvenile Grass Carp: Implications for Standardized Testing and Fish-Passage Design
pmc-13564652.creator: Jianzhang Lv, Jingjuan Li, Zixuan Li, Biao Wang, Yinzhu Liu, Huijuan Chen, Xiaogang Wang
pmc-13564652.description: Simple SummaryReliable measurements of how well fish swim are needed to design passages that help fish move past dams and other barriers. However, the size of the testing chamber may change the measured result. We tested young grass carp in chambers of different lengths and widths and also examined how water moved around the fish.

pmc-13625311.title: Towards routine biomechanical data collection in stroke rehabilitation: a usability comparison of IMU and markerless motion capture systems for functional upper-limb assessments
pmc-13625311.creator: Tim Unger, Xin Yao, Anna Schmitt, Lea Cebulla, Chris Easthope Awai
pmc-13625311.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective measurement of upper-limb movement quality based on biomechanical data collected in clinical routine has the potential to enable precision neurorehabilitation at scale. However, integrating biomechanical data collection into daily clinical workflows remains challenging. In this exploratory study, we evaluated the usability of two technologies for routine kinematic data collection: an IMU-based version of the instrumented Action Research Arm Test (iARAT-IMU) and a MMC markerless motion capture (MMC) system.
